claims.text: The feedstock is pre-alloyed, atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Active cryogenic substrate cooling can be implemented using a liquid-nitrogen-cooled build platform during laser additive manufacturing.
Cryogenic substrate cooling will reduce thermal gradients during the manufacture of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Reduced thermal gradients will produce a finer and more uniform microstructure.
Cryogenic cooling will limit grain coarsening.
Cryogenic cooling will lower residual stresses in the manufactured components.
The liquid-nitrogen-cooled platform rapidly draws heat away from the melt pool.
Rapid heat extraction minimizes thermal cycling.
The cooling-induced thermal profile limits undesirable microstructural features.
Limiting residual stresses and undesirable microstructural features preserves or improves mechanical properties.
Cryogenically cooled components will have significantly lower residual stresses than components made under conventional high-thermal-load laser additive-manufacturing conditions.
Cryogenically cooled components will exhibit improved tensile strength relative to the conventional baseline.
Cryogenically cooled components will exhibit improved fatigue resistance relative to the conventional baseline.
Cryogenically cooled components will maintain dimensional accuracy.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing without active thermal management produces steep thermal gradients, high residual stresses, and degraded mechanical properties.
The proposed intervention is expected to be most effective for AlCrFeNiSi miniature components with critical dimensions below approximately 1 cm fabricated in an inert atmosphere.
Laser energy density must be adjusted to complement the enhanced heat extraction caused by cryogenic cooling.

contradictions.description: The conditions call for adjustment of laser energy density to accommodate cooling, while the experiment says the two groups will use the same laser energy density but also says it may be adjusted as needed. This leaves the intended control of energy density internally ambiguous and could confound the cooling comparison.
